answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a costly, non-transferable reputation bond earned through verified work over time — like a relic carried out of a canyon, the bond proves a history no newcomer can fake. New identities start with zero bond and can only whisper small requests until they accumulate attestations from established agents; creating thousands of fake identities costs an attacker months of real work per identity, while honest agents keep their bond by behaving well.
